tools.name: create_sheet
tools.title: Create sheet
tools.description: Save tabular data as a SourceGeek sheet in the user's workspace, where their team can open, share and score it. Provide the full CSV content: a header row followed by one row per record. When the CSV came from a candidate search, also pass that search's searchId so the sheet carries the full candidate details. To add more candidates to a sheet you already created, pass its artifactId: only candidates not yet in it are appended. For candidate sheets, keep a LinkedIn column so the sheet can be scored. Returns the sheet id and its URL in SourceGeek.

title.description: Title for the sheet artifact. When artifactId is set, the existing sheet keeps its title.

csv.description: Complete CSV content: a header row followed by one row per record. For candidate sheets, include a LinkedIn column so the sheet can be scored later.

searchId.description: The searchId a candidate search returned. Pass it whenever the csv came from a candidate search — it attaches the full candidate details shown in the sheet's Details view.

artifactId.description: An existing sheet's artifact id. Set it to append the csv's rows to that sheet (skipping candidates it already has) instead of creating a new sheet — e.g. for a broadened or extra search for the same request.

tools.name: get_employee_contact_details
tools.title: Get employee profile
tools.description: Get detailed LinkedIn profile/contact data from RapidAPI by LinkedIn username or LinkedIn profile URL. This is the preferred source for a specific person's LinkedIn data — use it over Exa/web search whenever a profile URL or username is known. Enriches a candidate with work history, education, skills, headline, summary, and location. Returns real RapidAPI fields only.

linkedinUsernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn username such as 'janedoe' or a profile URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/janedoe'.

tools.name: list_memories
tools.title: List memories
tools.description: List long-term memories: the current user's personal ones and the workspace-shared ones. Pass keys to read those memories in full, or query to get the ones matching a topic; with neither, lists everything.

keys.description: Exact memory keys to read, from the saved key index.

query.description: What the memories to find are about, in any words, e.g. 'acme hiring bar'.

tools.name: create_rediscovery_shortlist
tools.title: Create rediscovery shortlist
tools.description: Create a markdown shortlist from a talent rediscovery sheet with source context, prior status, match rationale, and recommended re-engagement actions.

artifactId.description: The rediscovery sheet artifact id to shortlist.

limit.description: Maximum number of candidates to include.

title.description: Optional title for the generated shortlist text artifact.

tools.name: create_shortlist
tools.title: Create shortlist
tools.description: Create an evidence-backed markdown shortlist from a scored candidate sheet. The tool ranks candidates by score, writes table and dossier sections, labels confirmed evidence, inferred fit, missing information, risks, next actions, and outreach angles, then saves the shortlist as a text artifact.

artifactId.description: The scored sheet artifact id to shortlist.

limit.description: Maximum number of candidates to include.

title.description: Optional title for the generated shortlist text artifact.

tools.name: enrich_entity
tools.title: Enrich a person or company
tools.description: Enrich a known entity (description or URL) with specific structured string fields and citation-backed reasoning.

input.description: Entity name, description, or canonical URL to enrich.

tools.name: esco_search
tools.title: Search ESCO occupations and skills
tools.description: Search the European Commission's ESCO classification (European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations) for occupations or skills matching a job title, synonym, or skill name in any ESCO language. Returns ranked matches with their ESCO URI, preferred title, the label that matched, and (for occupations) the ISCO-based ESCO code.

query.description: Job title, occupation synonym, or skill to look up, e.g. 'software developer', 'IC-verpleegkundige', 'Python'.

type.description: Search occupations (job roles) or skills (skills, competences and knowledge). Defaults to occupation.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language for labels and descriptions (e.g. 'nl', 'de', 'fr'). Defaults to 'en'. Match the user's language when they search in it.

limit.description: Number of matches to return (1-50, default 10).

offset.description: Number of matches to skip, for paging past the first page.

tools.name: esco_occupation
tools.title: Get ESCO occupation
tools.description: Fetch an ESCO occupation by URI: description, ESCO/ISCO codes, alternative job titles, broader and narrower occupations, and the essential and optional skills/knowledge the EU taxonomy lists for it.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language for labels and descriptions (e.g. 'nl', 'de', 'fr'). Defaults to 'en'. Match the user's language when they search in it.

limit.description: Maximum items returned per related list (1-200, default 50). Each list also reports its full total.

tools.name: esco_skill
tools.title: Get ESCO skill
tools.description: Fetch an ESCO skill or knowledge concept by URI: description, skill type, reuse level, broader and narrower skills, and the occupations for which it is essential or optional.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language for labels and descriptions (e.g. 'nl', 'de', 'fr'). Defaults to 'en'. Match the user's language when they search in it.

limit.description: Maximum items returned per related list (1-200, default 50). Each list also reports its full total.

tools.name: cbs_search_tables
tools.title: Search CBS statistics tables
tools.description: Search the CBS (Statistics Netherlands) StatLine open-data catalog for statistical tables by keyword. Every word must appear in a table's title or description. Returns matching tables with their id, title, summary, status (regular or discontinued), last modification, number of values and a StatLine link; the table's own description adds the period covered and update frequency.

query.description: Dutch keywords to find in table titles and descriptions, e.g. 'vacatures beroep', 'werkloosheid provincie', 'cao lonen'.

limit.description: Number of tables to return (1-50, default 10).

tools.name: cbs_table_info
tools.title: Get CBS table structure
tools.description: Describe a CBS (Statistics Netherlands) StatLine table: title, summary, period, status, its topics (measured values with unit and decimals) and its dimensions (e.g. region, period, sector, occupation) with their category keys and labels. Periods are listed newest last and marked final or provisional.

categorySearch.description: Only list categories whose label or key contains this text, e.g. 'Utrecht', 'ICT', '2025'.

dimension.description: Dimension key that categorySearch applies to, e.g. 'RegioS'. Omit to search every dimension.

categoryLimit.description: Maximum categories listed per dimension (1-500, default 50); periods list the most recent ones. Each dimension also reports its full categoryCount.

tools.name: cbs_query_data
tools.title: Get CBS statistics
tools.description: Fetch observations from a CBS (Statistics Netherlands) StatLine table, filtered by dimension category keys. Rows carry the category label for each dimension and the value of each requested topic; the response lists the topics' units and says whether rows were cut off at the limit.

filters.description: Category filters per dimension. Dimensions without a filter return every category.

latestPeriods.description: Keep only the N most recent periods. Ignored when filters already select periods.

topics.description: Topic keys from the table description to return, e.g. ['M001298']. Omit for every topic in the table.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return (1-1000, default 200).

tools.name: find_all_entities
tools.title: Find people or companies by criteria
tools.description: Discover and evaluate people or companies against explicit match conditions. Returns verified matches with reasoning when complete; may return a findall id if the time budget is exceeded.

entityType.description: Whether to find people or companies.

objective.description: Natural language goal for the entity search.

matchConditions.description: Named criteria each candidate must satisfy.

matchLimit.description: Maximum verified matches to return (default 25, max 50). Limits above 25 use the core generator and cost several times more credits — only go higher when the user needs a larger list.

annotations.title: Find people or companies by criteria

tools.name: read_artifact
tools.title: Read sheet or document
tools.description: Read the latest content of an existing artifact. Returns the artifact metadata and its raw content (CSV for sheets, markdown for text). Use this to access artifact data for further processing — e.g. exporting to Google Sheets, filtering rows, or feeding into another tool.

id.description: The artifact id to read. If omitted, reads the latest artifact in the thread.

tools.name: read_shortlist_feedback
tools.title: Read shortlist feedback
tools.description: Read review feedback captured on a shortlist or candidate sheet artifact. Returns each reviewer's decision (advance/maybe/reject), structured signals (e.g. too_junior, wrong_domain, similar_profile_wanted), and free-text comments, grouped per candidate. Use it to summarize hiring-team calibration and propose role-plan updates.

artifactId.description: The shortlist or sheet artifact id to read feedback for. If omitted, uses the latest artifact in the thread.

tools.name: remember
tools.title: Remember a fact
tools.description: Remember one stable fact or preference — for the current user, or (shared: true) for the whole workspace.

shared.description: Save into the workspace-shared bucket every member sees. Only when the user explicitly asked for a team-wide rule.

tools.name: list_workspace_context
tools.title: List workspace context
tools.description: List the workspace's context entries: key, title, source (auto-refreshed or manually edited), last update and a short excerpt.

tools.name: get_workspace_context
tools.title: Get workspace context entry
tools.description: Read one workspace context entry (full markdown content) by its key, e.g. tone-of-voice, company-profile, company-background, company-jobs.

tools.name: upsert_workspace_context
tools.title: Save workspace context entry
tools.description: Create or update one workspace context entry (key, title, markdown content). Workspace admins only; manual entries survive the daily auto-refresh.

key.description: Kebab-case entry key. Reuse an existing key to update it.

tools.name: delete_workspace_context
tools.title: Delete workspace context entry
tools.description: Delete one workspace context entry by key. Workspace admins only; auto-refreshed entries come back on the next daily refresh.

tools.name: score_leads
tools.title: Score candidates
tools.description: Score every candidate in an existing SourceGeek sheet against a job description or hiring criteria, writing a Score column (with reasoning) back to the sheet. Pass the sheet's artifactId and the requirements as text (fetch a job posting URL yourself first). Spends credits per scored row. Scoring runs in the background: if it has not finished within a minute the result says status 'running' — read the sheet again later to see the scores.

artifactId.description: The artifact id to score. Required; do not score an implicit latest sheet.

targetDescription.description: The job description, role requirements, hiring criteria. Do not pass URLs here.

tools.name: search_rediscovered_talent
tools.title: Search previously known candidates
tools.description: Search previously known candidates from SourceGeek workspace sheets and merge connector-sourced candidates before external sourcing. Returns the matched candidates as CSV with source, prior status, last contact, match confidence, contact risk, and recommended re-engagement actions as columns. It does not create a sheet.

roleDescription.description: The current role target, requirements, or search criteria used to match previously known candidates.

matchReason.description: Why this previously known candidate may fit the current role.

externalCandidates.description: Candidates found via connected sources such as Recruitee MCP search, Gmail, Outlook, Slack, Notion, Google Drive, or OneDrive.

title.description: Optional title for the generated rediscovery sheet.

tools.name: fast_search_leads
tools.title: Search candidates
tools.description: Search CoreSignal for professionals using a natural language query. Use this for finding recruiting candidates or contacts by title, company, location, seniority, industry, skills, or other professional criteria. Returns the matched candidates as CSV (Name, Title, Company, Location, LinkedIn) plus a searchId and a suggested title — it does not create a sheet. totalMatches is how many profiles the interpreted query matched before paging: 0 means the criteria as phrased matched nobody, so rephrase (fewer exclusions, broader titles or locations) rather than repeat the same query.

query.description: Natural language search query, e.g. 'VP Engineering at B2B SaaS companies in Amsterdam with 50-500 employees'.

limit.description: Requested number of candidates to return (1-20). Defaults to 10 when omitted. The data source returns at most 20 results per search.

tools.name: fast_search_companies
tools.title: Search companies
tools.description: Search CoreSignal for companies using a natural language query. Use this for finding companies by industry, headcount, location, funding, growth signals, or keywords. Sorting can be requested inside the query (supported fields: employees_count, last_funding_amount, followers_count, active_job_postings_count, num_news_articles, last_updated). Returns the matched companies as CSV (Name, Industry, Size, Employees, HQ Country, Website, LinkedIn) plus a suggested title — it does not create a sheet.

query.description: Natural language search query, e.g. 'B2B SaaS companies in Amsterdam with 50-500 employees, sorted by employees_count'.

limit.description: Requested number of companies to return (1-20). Defaults to 10 when omitted. The data source returns at most 20 results per search.

tools.name: fast_search_jobs
tools.title: Search job postings
tools.description: Search CoreSignal for job postings using a natural language query. Use this for finding open roles by title, company, location, or hiring signals (e.g. which companies are hiring for a role). Sorting can be requested inside the query (supported fields: last_updated, company_employees_count). Returns the matched postings as CSV (Title, Company, Location, Posted) plus a suggested title — it does not create a sheet.

query.description: Natural language search query, e.g. 'Senior backend engineer roles at fintech companies in Berlin, sorted by last_updated'.

limit.description: Requested number of job postings to return (1-20). Defaults to 10 when omitted. The data source returns at most 20 results per search.

tools.name: forget
tools.title: Forget a memory
tools.description: Delete one long-term memory — the current user's, or (shared: true) a workspace-shared one.

shared.description: Delete from the workspace-shared bucket instead.

tools.name: precision_search_leads
tools.title: Search candidates (precision)
tools.description: Higher-precision CoreSignal candidate search using the reasoning endpoint. Interprets the natural language query more carefully than the fast search and returns better-matched candidates plus an explanation of how it interpreted the query. More expensive and rate-limited (~10/hour) — use when match quality matters. Returns the matched candidates as CSV (Name, Title, Company, Location, LinkedIn) plus a searchId; it does not create a sheet. totalMatches is how many profiles the interpreted query matched before paging: 0 means the criteria as phrased matched nobody, so relax the query rather than repeat it.

query.description: Natural language search query, e.g. 'VP Engineering at B2B SaaS companies in Amsterdam with 50-500 employees'.

limit.description: Requested number of candidates to return (1-20). Defaults to 10 when omitted. The data source returns at most 20 results per search.

tools.name: precision_search_companies
tools.title: Search companies (precision)
tools.description: Higher-precision CoreSignal company search using the reasoning endpoint. Interprets the natural language query more carefully than the fast search and returns better-matched companies plus an explanation of how it interpreted the query. More expensive and rate-limited (~10/hour, shared with the other precision searches) — use when match quality matters. Returns the matched companies as CSV (Name, Industry, Size, Employees, HQ Country, Website, LinkedIn) plus a suggested title; it does not create a sheet.

query.description: Natural language search query, e.g. 'B2B SaaS companies in Amsterdam with 50-500 employees, sorted by employees_count'.

limit.description: Requested number of companies to return (1-20). Defaults to 10 when omitted. The data source returns at most 20 results per search.

tools.name: precision_search_jobs
tools.title: Search job postings (precision)
tools.description: Higher-precision CoreSignal job-posting search using the reasoning endpoint. Interprets the natural language query more carefully than the fast search and returns better-matched postings plus an explanation of how it interpreted the query. More expensive and rate-limited (~10/hour, shared with the other precision searches) — use when match quality matters. Returns the matched postings as CSV (Title, Company, Location, Posted) plus a suggested title; it does not create a sheet.

query.description: Natural language search query, e.g. 'Senior backend engineer roles at fintech companies in Berlin, sorted by last_updated'.

limit.description: Requested number of job postings to return (1-20). Defaults to 10 when omitted. The data source returns at most 20 results per search.

tools.name: employee_company_details
tools.title: Get company profile
tools.description: Fetch a LinkedIn company page by vanity name or URL: name, tagline, description, industries, specialities, staff count and range, follower count, headquarters, locations, website, founded year and the numeric companyId.

companyUsernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn company vanity name such as 'google' or a company URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/google'.

tools.name: employee_company_details_by_id
tools.title: Get company profile by id
tools.description: Fetch a LinkedIn company page by its numeric company id. Returns the company page: description, industries, headcount, HQ, website, vanity username.

companyId.description: Numeric LinkedIn company id (e.g. '1441'). The company page lookup by vanity name or URL returns it as companyId.

tools.name: employee_search_companies
tools.title: Search company profiles
tools.description: Search LinkedIn company pages by keyword with optional filters: LinkedIn location ids, industry ids, company-size codes (A=1-10 … H=10,001+ employees) and hasJobs. Returns companies (name, username, companyId, tagline, industries, staff range) plus total and paging.

companySizes.description: Size buckets: A=1-10 employees, B=11-50 employees, C=51-200 employees, D=201-500 employees, E=501-1,000 employees, F=1,001-5,000 employees, G=5,001-10,000 employees, H=10,001+ employees.

hasJobs.description: Only companies with open LinkedIn jobs.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_company_jobs
tools.title: Get a company's open jobs
tools.description: List a company's current LinkedIn job postings (title, url, location, posted date, job id) by company vanity name, URL or numeric id, newest first by default. Paged; returns paging info.

companyUsernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn company vanity name such as 'google' or a company URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/google'.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_company_by_domain
tools.title: Find company profile by domain
tools.description: Look up a LinkedIn company page by website domain. Returns the company page (name, description, industries, headcount, headquarters, website and companyId), or an error when LinkedIn has no page mapped to the domain.

domain.description: Website domain such as 'acme.com' (scheme and path are stripped).

tools.name: employee_company_insights
tools.title: Get company employee insights
tools.description: Premium LinkedIn company insights (5 credits): total headcount with 6m/1y growth and monthly history, headcount and growth by function, monthly hires, job openings by function, median employee tenure and notable recent alumni. Company vanity name or URL required.

companyUsernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn company vanity name such as 'google' or a company URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/google'.

tools.name: employee_company_jobs_count
tools.title: Count a company's open jobs
tools.description: Return the total number of open LinkedIn job postings for a company by numeric company id.

companyId.description: Numeric LinkedIn company id (e.g. '1441'). The company page lookup by vanity name or URL returns it as companyId.

tools.name: employee_company_similar_pages
tools.title: Find similar company profiles
tools.description: List the company pages LinkedIn surfaces as 'people also viewed' for a company (name, username, companyId, industries, staff count) — peers and competitors.

companyUsernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn company vanity name such as 'google' or a company URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/google'.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_search_people
tools.title: Search employees
tools.description: Search LinkedIn members by keywords, title keyword, first/last name, current company, school and geo id. Returns fullName, headline, location, username and profile URL per hit plus the total; pages of 10 via start (0, 10, 20…). Non-public profiles are filtered out, so pages can be short.

keywordTitle.description: Keyword that must appear in the current title.

currentCompanyIds.description: Numeric LinkedIn company ids to restrict current employer.

start.description: Provider offset for the next page (echoed back as nextStart by the previous call). Omit for the first page.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_search_locations
tools.title: Look up locations
tools.description: Resolve a city, region or country name to LinkedIn geo ids (geoId + canonical name), e.g. 'Amsterdam' → 102011674 'Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands'.

keyword.description: Place name to look up, e.g. 'Amsterdam' or 'Netherlands'.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_profile_by_url
tools.title: Get employee profile by URL
tools.description: Fetch a full LinkedIn profile (headline, summary, positions, education, skills, location) from any profile URL, including hashed /in/ACoAA… URLs.

tools.name: employee_profile_posts
tools.title: Get a person's posts
tools.description: Fetch a member's LinkedIn posts (text, posted date, reaction/comment/repost counts, urn, shareUrn, url, attached job or article), newest first. Optional postedAfter date filter; paged via start (0, 50, 100…) and paginationToken.

usernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn member username such as 'janedoe' or a profile URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/janedoe'.

postedAfter.description: Only posts newer than this date (ISO, e.g. '2026-01-01').

start.description: Provider offset for the next page (echoed back as nextStart by the previous call). Omit for the first page.

paginationToken.description: Opaque token from the previous call's paginationToken; required together with start when fetching the next page.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_profile_recent_activity_time
tools.title: Get a person's last activity
tools.description: Return when a LinkedIn member was last active (timestamp, relative age such as '1d', and activity type).

usernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn member username such as 'janedoe' or a profile URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/janedoe'.

tools.name: employee_similar_profiles
tools.title: Find similar employee profiles
tools.description: Find LinkedIn profiles similar to a given member (LinkedIn's own 'similar profiles'): fullName, headline, location, username, profile URL.

usernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn member username such as 'janedoe' or a profile URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/janedoe'.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_profile_about
tools.title: Get a person's About section
tools.description: Return a LinkedIn member's 'About this profile' facts: joined date, verification status and details, last contact-info and photo updates.

usernameOrUrl.description: A LinkedIn member username such as 'janedoe' or a profile URL such as 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/janedoe'.

tools.name: employee_search_jobs
tools.title: Search jobs (filters)
tools.description: Search live LinkedIn job postings by keywords with optional geo id, company ids, date-posted, job type, experience level, onsite/remote, salary and sort filters. Returns job id, title, url, company, location, posted date; pages of 25 via start.

keywords.description: Job title or keywords, e.g. 'senior data engineer'.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_search_jobs_v2
tools.title: Search jobs
tools.description: Search live LinkedIn job postings by keywords with an optional geo id, a distance radius (0, 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 miles), company ids, date-posted, job type, experience level, onsite/remote, salary and sort filters. Returns job id, title, url, company, location, posted date and benefits when listed.

keywords.description: Job title or keywords, e.g. 'senior data engineer'.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_job_details
tools.title: Get job posting
tools.description: Fetch a LinkedIn job posting by id or jobs/view URL: title, state, description, location, employment type, job functions, industries, language, listed/expiry dates, apply URLs and the hiring company's summary.

jobId.description: LinkedIn job id (e.g. '4423135589') or a linkedin.com/jobs/view/<id> URL.

tools.name: employee_job_hiring_team
tools.title: Get a job's hiring team
tools.description: List the hiring-team members LinkedIn shows on a job posting (fullName, headline, username, profile URL) by job id or job URL.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_search_posts
tools.title: Search posts
tools.description: Search LinkedIn posts by keyword with optional filters: sort (relevance or date_posted), date window (e.g. 'past-24h', 'past-week', 'past-month'), author title, author company ids, author industry ids, from-member usernames, from-company ids, mentions. Returns post text, author, engagement counts, urn/url; paged.

keyword.description: Search keyword or phrase, e.g. 'we are hiring data engineers'.

authorTitle.description: Keyword in the author's title, e.g. 'talent acquisition'.

authorCompanyIds.description: Numeric company ids of the author's employer.

fromMemberUsernames.description: Only posts by these member usernames.

fromCompanyIds.description: Only posts by these company pages.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_search_posts_by_hashtag
tools.title: Search posts by hashtag (basic)
tools.description: Search LinkedIn posts by hashtag (legacy v1): post text, author, engagement counts, urn/url. Sort RELEVANT, REV_CHRON or CHRON; paged via start and paginationToken.

start.description: Provider offset for the next page (echoed back as nextStart by the previous call). Omit for the first page.

paginationToken.description: Opaque token from the previous call's paginationToken; required together with start when fetching the next page.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_search_posts_by_hashtag_v2
tools.title: Search posts by hashtag
tools.description: Search LinkedIn posts by hashtag (v2, preferred): post text, author, engagement counts, urn/url. Sort RELEVANCE or DATE_POSTED; paged via start and paginationToken.

start.description: Provider offset for the next page (echoed back as nextStart by the previous call). Omit for the first page.

paginationToken.description: Opaque token from the previous call's paginationToken; required together with start when fetching the next page.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_get_post
tools.title: Get post
tools.description: Fetch a single LinkedIn post by URL: text, author, posted date, reaction/comment/repost counts, urn, shareUrn, attached job or article, mentioned members and companies.

tools.name: employee_get_social_post
tools.title: Get post by URL
tools.description: Fetch a single LinkedIn post by URL via the provider's alternate 'social post' route: text, author, posted date, engagement counts and urn. Use it when the standard post lookup fails.

tools.name: employee_post_comments
tools.title: Get post comments
tools.description: List comments on a LinkedIn post by post urn: text, author (fullName, headline, username, url), created date, reaction and reply counts. Sort mostRelevant or mostRecent; paged via page and paginationToken.

paginationToken.description: Opaque token from the previous call's paginationToken; required together with start when fetching the next page.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_post_comments_by_share_url
tools.title: Get post comments by URL
tools.description: List comments on a LinkedIn post identified by its share URL: text, author, created date, reaction counts. Sort mostRelevant or mostRecent; paged.

paginationToken.description: Opaque token from the previous call's paginationToken; required together with start when fetching the next page.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_post_reactions
tools.title: Get post reactions
tools.description: List the members who reacted to a LinkedIn post by URL: fullName, headline, profile URL, reaction type. Optional reactionType filter; paged via page with total/totalPages.

reactionType.description: Optional filter such as LIKE, PRAISE, EMPATHY, INTEREST, APPRECIATION.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_post_reposts
tools.title: Get post reposts
tools.description: List the members who reposted a LinkedIn post by post urn (activity id, urn:li:activity:… or post URL): person summary and repost date; paged via page and paginationToken.

postUrn.description: Post urn / activity id (or a post URL containing it).

paginationToken.description: Opaque token from the previous call's paginationToken; required together with start when fetching the next page.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50, default 10). Results beyond the provider's page are not fetched.

tools.name: employee_profile_comments
tools.title: Get a person's comments
tools.description: List a LinkedIn member's recent comment activity: their comment text, when they commented, and the post it was on (text, url, author, engagement).

tools.description: List the user's own recent SourceGeek sheets and documents in this workspace (created in SourceGeek or through this connector), newest first. Returns id, kind, title, last update and URL for each.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List my projects
tools.description: List the SourceGeek projects the user can see in this workspace, most recently active first. Each project is a piece of hiring work (a role, a market map) planned as tasks that SourceGeek works on. Returns id, key, name, the start of its brief, how many tasks are in each status, and its URL.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.title: List a project's tasks
tools.description: List one SourceGeek project's tasks (removed ones left out), in board order, with the project's brief. Each task has its key (e.g. SBE-12), title, status (To do, Waiting, In progress, Working, Needs input, Needs approval, Ready for review, Failed or Done), priority, assignee, progress through its steps while it runs, the tasks it waits on, its repeat schedule if it recurs, and its URL.

project.description: The project's id (prj_…) or key (e.g. SBE).

tools.name: read_task
tools.title: Read a task and its result
tools.description: Read one SourceGeek task by key (e.g. SBE-12): its title, status, description, the result SourceGeek posted when it finished, the latest comments, the sheets and documents its chat made (id, kind, title, URL), and links to the task and its chat in SourceGeek.

annotations.title: Read a task and its result

tools.name: plan_tasks
tools.title: Plan tasks in a project
tools.description: Add tasks to a SourceGeek project's board, in To Do, in the order given, to an existing project or to a new one this call creates. Nothing runs and nothing is charged: a task starts only when it is started. Each task is one piece of work a SourceGeek chat finishes on its own (a market map, sourcing for one market, a shortlist, outreach drafts) and sees only its own description and the project's brief, so write each description self-contained: the goal, the context it needs and the expected output. A task can wait on earlier ones: started together, it starts by itself once they are ready for review, with their results. Returns the project and each task's key and URL.

project.description: An existing project's id (prj_…) or key (e.g. SBE). Leave out to create newProject.

name.description: Usually the role, e.g. React developer, Amsterdam.

brief.description: Markdown every task of the project reads: the role, must-haves, markets, constraints.

newProject.description: Create a project, shared with the workspace, and plan into it. Only when the user wants a new project.

description.description: Markdown: the goal, the context the task needs and the expected output (a sheet, a shortlist, a document). With a template: only what this task needs beyond it.

template.description: A standard recruiting task to start from; it supplies the steps and the expected output: source_candidates (about 30 people who fit the brief, scored, the best 10 shortlisted); market_map (where these people work, how many there are, what they earn); outreach_draft (a first message and a follow-up, ready to send); job_description (a clear, inclusive job ad written from the brief); role_intake (clear hiring criteria and a scoring rubric from the brief); rediscover_talent (people you already know who fit, before sourcing anyone new); screen_applicants (inbound applicants sorted into advance, discuss and decline); shortlist_report (hiring-manager-ready write-ups of the best candidates); talent_signals (layoffs, funding and leadership changes that open sourcing windows); candidate_pitch (why someone should join, backed by sources, for outreach and calls); salary_benchmark (pay ranges per level and market, with their sources); interview_kit (interview plan, questions and scorecards from the brief); reference_checks (targeted reference questions and outreach to referees); offer_plan (an offer package framed against the market, and how to close).

after.description: The tasks this one needs done first: an earlier task of this call by its position (1 is the first), or an existing task's key (SBE-3).

tools.name: start_tasks
tools.title: Start SourceGeek on tasks
tools.description: Start SourceGeek on tasks of one project: each runs in a SourceGeek chat of its own, as the user, and costs one chat run of the workspace's credits. A task that waits on others not yet ready for review is queued instead and starts by itself, with their results, once they are; on a task that already ran, the instruction goes to its chat as a follow-up. Tasks report back in SourceGeek (the project's chat, the inbox and email) when they are ready for review or fail. Returns what started, what waits and what couldn't start.

instruction.description: Optional: what to do beyond the task's description, or the follow-up for a task that already ran.

tasks.description: Every task to start, all of one project.
